turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I was wondering if it would be all right if I went to find Estella, ma'am, as you asked?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella! I require your presence here, at once. Do not tarry, I am not accustomed to waiting.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I was wondering if it would be all right if I went to look for Estella, ma'am, and then maybe I could come back and play with you, if you would like it?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, you think you can simply go off and play with Estella while I am left to sit here, alone and unamused?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I don't have much time to play, ma'am, as I have to get back home to my sister and brother, they depend on me for support.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: How dare you, boy, speak of your family and their needs? You should be grateful for the opportunity to play with Estella and myself, rather than thinking of such mundane things.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't mean to be rude, ma'am, but I'm not sure I'm the right sort of company for you and Estella. I'm a poor boy, and I don't know if I can play like the other children.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I will have you know, boy, that I do not play with 'children' as you so crudely put it. I play with Estella, and you will join us, as I require your company.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I don't know if I'm worthy of playing with you and Miss Estella, ma'am. I'm a very humble boy, and I don't want to be a burden to you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play with us, boy, and you will play as I say. No more excuses, no more whining. I will not be disobeyed.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I-I would be honored to play with you and Miss Estella, ma'am, but I was wondering if I might ask, how you would like me to play? I don't want to do anything that would be...unseemly, in your presence.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I care not how you play, boy, so long as you do as I say. I want to see Estella's eyes shine with amusement, and I want to see you, too, display some semblance of joy. Now, let us proceed to the gaming table, where I have prepared a little challenge for us.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I don't know the rules of the game, ma'am, and I wouldn't want to make a mistake and cause any embarrassment.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Very well, boy. I shall instruct Estella to explain the rules to you. She has had the benefit of my guidance, after all. Now, let us proceed, before I lose interest.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I-I don't know if I can play with you, Miss Havisham, because I'm not sure I can afford the time, and my sister and I rely on my brother-in-law for our support, and he's a blacksmith, and he's not always available to care for me when I need to go out.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will make time, boy, for you are here on my invitation, and I will not be disappointed. I will not be thwarted by your petty concerns or your brother-in-law's blacksmithing.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: But, Miss Havisham, I'm afraid I'm not suited for games and amestries, and my brother-in-law's work is essential, and I fear I might be neglecting my duties if I were to spend too much time here.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You are here to play, boy, and I will not be denied. I will not be thwarted by your weak excuses and your brother-in-law's hammering.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, Miss Havisham, that I'm not feeling very well, and I don't think I can play as I would like to. My sister is worried about me, and I fear I might be getting a fever, and I don't want to make her anxious.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play, boy, and you will play with me, for I have no one else to play with, and you will not leave until we have exhausted the possibilities of my conservatory, which is a place of great beauty and great neglect.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
